Benchmark decomposition of a disparity

Source: R/disp.R
dspbm.Rd

Splits each group's disparity in force per resident, against a reference group, into a disparity in contact per resident times a disparity in force per contact. The split is a product, never a sum. See proof("dspbm").

Usage

dspbm(pop, contact, force, ref = 1)

Arguments

pop

Residents by group: positive numbers, optionally named.

contact

Police contacts by group: positive numbers, same length.

force

Uses of force by group: positive numbers, same length.

ref

The reference group, by name (matched exactly, case included) or position.

Value

A data frame with one row per group: group, cd (contact per resident), fd (force per contact) and rd (force per resident), each against the reference group, with rd = cd * fd.

Examples

dspbm(pop = c(a = 9000, b = 1000), contact = c(a = 900, b = 300),
      force = c(a = 9, b = 6))
#>   group cd fd rd
#> 1     a  1  1  1
#> 2     b  3  2  6
